The raw_merchants table holds 46 rows for 40 distinct merchant_ids. Six ids appear twice, and the copies are identical in every column. The join in gold_mcc_daily therefore fans out and inflates the count (5416 vs 4699). Deduplicating silver_merchants fixes it with no ambiguity, because the copies are exact duplicates.

A check on the numbers: 5416 − 4699 = 717 extra rows, which is plausible for 6 duplicated merchants out of 40.

The fix is to use SELECT DISTINCT in silver_merchants, which keeps the same columns. Other tables are unaffected. gold_merchant_daily does not join merchants, so it is fine.

The reconciliation also assumes silver_transactions (POSTED only) is the intended base. The REVERSED rows are excluded by design and the alert compares against silver, so no change is needed there.
